items.text: Vector2/3/4::Divide(v, s), operator/(v, s) and Matrix::Divide(m, s) divide each component by s, whereas XNA 4.0 multiplies by one reciprocal 1/s; Vector3::operator/= alone uses the reciprocal and its comment wrongly says Divide does too, so v / s, v /= s and XNA's v / s can differ in the last bit.
items.evidence: modules/math/src/Vector2.cpp, Vector3.cpp, Vector4.cpp, Matrix.cpp (Divide, operator/=); XNA 4.0 IL (Vector3::Divide, op_Division, Matrix.Divide)

items.text: Ray::Intersects(BoundingBox) returns no hit for a zero-direction ray whose origin is inside the box (XNA returns 0), uses a 2^-24 parallel threshold where XNA uses 1e-6, and divides where XNA multiplies by a reciprocal.
Ray::Intersects(BoundingSphere) treats only a strictly inside origin as a hit at 0 (XNA uses <=), so a ray starting exactly on the surface and pointing outward returns no hit in CNA and 0 in XNA.
BoundingSphere::Contains(Vector3) returns Intersects for a point exactly on the surface; XNA 4.0 returns Contains only for d^2 < r^2 and Disjoint otherwise (never Intersects).

BoundingSphere::Contains(BoundingSphere) tests d^2 <= (R - r)^2, which loses the sign of R - r, so a larger argument sphere enclosing this one is reported as Contains (e.g. radius 1 containing a concentric radius 5); XNA tests R - r >= d and answers Intersects. Ported from FNA.

BoundingFrustum::Intersects(BoundingBox) and Intersects(BoundingSphere) are Contains(...) != Disjoint, a conservative per-plane test that reports true for volumes beside a frustum edge or corner; XNA 4.0 uses an exact GJK query. BoundingBox/BoundingSphere::Intersects(frustum) and the engine-layer culling helpers inherit it.
items.evidence: modules/math/src/BoundingFrustum.cpp (Intersects overloads, Contains); XNA 4.0 BoundingFrustum.Intersects(ref BoundingBox/ref BoundingSphere) with Gjk

items.text: BoundingFrustum::Intersects(Plane) classifies corners with Plane::IntersectsPoint, so a corner exactly on the plane counts as Intersecting; XNA counts a zero distance as Back, so a frustum touching a plane from behind is Back in XNA and Intersecting in CNA.

Ray::ToString and BoundingBox::ToString emit literal doubled braces ({{Min:... }}) copied from FNA's string concatenation; XNA formats the same text with string.Format, which yields single braces. BoundingBoxTest.ToStringMatchesFNAFormat pins the FNA form, contrary to the project's XNA-over-FNA rule.
items.evidence: modules/math/src/BoundingBox.cpp, Ray.cpp (ToString); modules/math/tests/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/BoundingBoxTests.cpp; XNA 4.0 BoundingBox/Ray.ToString; FNA b355124 src/BoundingBox.cs

items.text: Math ToString numbers use std::ostringstream defaults (six significant digits, C++ global locale) while XNA formats with Single.ToString(CurrentCulture); only Matrix::ToString's outer format was measured against XNA.

The FloatHash used by Vector2/3/4, Matrix, Quaternion (and CurveKey) hashes raw float bits, so values that compare equal (+0.0f vs -0.0f components) get different hash codes; .NET Single.GetHashCode returns 0 for both zeros, keeping XNA's hashes consistent with Equals.
items.evidence: modules/math/src/Vector3.cpp (FloatHash, GetHashCode); Matrix.cpp; Quaternion.cpp; mscorlib IL Single::GetHashCode

items.text: Point declares operator+, -, * and / (component-wise, no divide-by-zero guard), which XNA 4.0's Point does not have, without the CNAEXT marker, so CNA_STRICT_XNA_API does not flag them.

items.section: Color is packed, named, and polymorphic
items.text: Color::FromNonPremultiplied(intcs r, g, b, a) computes r * a / 255 in 32-bit int; XNA multiplies in 64-bit long and clamps, so arguments whose product exceeds INT_MAX overflow (undefined behaviour) in CNA.

BoundingSphere::CreateFromBoundingBox computes (Min+Max)/2 and Distance(center, Max) where XNA computes Lerp(Min, Max, 0.5) and Distance(Min, Max)*0.5; last-bit agreement is unmeasured (the sphere oracle covers CreateFromPoints only).

MathHelper::SmoothStep/Hermite/CatmullRom (double, endpoint shortcuts) and the vector SmoothStep/Hermite (float Hermite basis) use different arithmetic from XNA's float Lerp(t^2(3-2t)) and Hermite forms; last-bit agreement is unmeasured and no oracle covers them.

MathHelper::MachineEpsilonFloat is a dynamically initialised static, so a static initialiser in another translation unit calling WithinEpsilon could observe 0; no such in-tree static consumer was found. Documentation caveat, recorded for completeness.
